rule_text: A data controller shall ensure that personal data is collected only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.
A data controller shall obtain the consent of the data subject before collecting or processing personal data.
Personal data shall be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.
A data controller shall ensure that personal data is accurate and where necessary kept up to date.
Personal data shall not be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data is processed.
A data controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security of personal data.
A data controller must ensure that personal data is protected against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage.
A data controller shall use encryption to protect personal data stored in electronic form.
A data controller shall notify the Commission and affected data subjects of a personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach.
A data subject shall have the right to request access to their personal data held by a data controller.
A data controller must provide a means by which data subjects can request correction of inaccurate personal data.
A data subject shall have the right to request the deletion of their personal data and the data controller must comply where the data is no longer necessary.
Personal data shall not be transferred to a foreign country unless that country provides an adequate level of data protection.
A data controller must ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place before transferring personal data to a third party organisation.
A data controller shall not sell personal data of data subjects to third parties without explicit consent.
A data controller shall provide clear and transparent information to data subjects about how their personal data is collected and used.
A data controller must publish a privacy policy that clearly explains the purpose of data collection and the rights of data subjects.
A data controller shall appoint a Data Protection Officer where the organisation processes large volumes of personal data.
A data controller shall conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment before processing personal data that is likely to result in high risk to data subjects.
Personal data relating to children shall not be processed without the consent of a parent or legal guardian.
A data controller shall implement access controls to ensure that personal data is only accessible to authorised personnel.
A data controller must maintain logs of all access to personal data to enable auditing and accountability.
A data controller shall not process sensitive personal data including health data, biometric data and financial data without explicit consent.
A data controller must have a lawful basis for every instance of personal data processing.
A data controller shall allow data subjects to withdraw their consent at any time and must stop processing their data upon withdrawal.
